claims.text: Grain-boundary density is the primary governor of first-order magnetostructural-transition width in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi HEA ribbons.
Grain-boundary density is the primary governor of thermal and magnetic hysteresis in these ribbons.
Grain boundaries act as heterogeneous nucleation sites that lower the phase-transformation energy barrier.
Changing grain-boundary density does not substantially alter the bulk entropy change.
The initial ribbons are as-deposited, melt-spun, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi HEAs.
The initial ribbons have a single-phase hexagonal structure.
The initial average grain size is approximately 200 nm.
Annealing at 400, 600, and 800 °C for 2 h can systematically vary grain size while preserving overall composition and phase structure.
Grain-boundary density is inversely related to average grain size.
Increasing grain-boundary area provides more martensitic-transformation nucleation sites.
The additional nucleation sites reduce activation energy and narrow hysteresis.
Reducing average grain size from approximately 5 µm to 50 nm will decrease thermal and magnetic hysteresis width by up to approximately 4 K.
Reducing average grain size from approximately 5 µm to 50 nm will broaden the transformation-temperature range by approximately 3 K.
The peak isothermal entropy change at 1.5 T will decrease by less than 10% over the predicted grain-size change.
The baseline ribbons have a thermal hysteresis width of approximately 10 K.
The baseline peak entropy change is approximately 12 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ under 1.5 T.
Below approximately 50 nm, ferromagnetic order weakens and the entropy change may fall below 8 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.
Above approximately 5 µm, hysteresis approaches or exceeds the baseline and is approximately 9 K or greater.

contradictions.description: The material is described as as-deposited, but the stated as-deposited baseline is also described as annealed at 400 °C. Post-deposition annealing is not an as-deposited condition.

The mechanism predicts nearly unchanged entropy change, and the uncertainty permits changes of ±1 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, yet the falsification rule says entropy-change invariance beyond ±1 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ would falsify the hypothesis. Invariance should instead be consistent with the stated mechanism.
The baseline hysteresis is stated as approximately 10 K, whereas the boundary describes approximately 9 K as approaching or exceeding baseline; 9 K does not exceed a 10 K baseline.
